key_insight: Combining 3D welding simulations with neural networks mapped HDPE weld-quality windows, identifying 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating as optimal within the tested conditions.
engineering_relevance: Bottom preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to about 1100 N and moderated thermal gradients, supporting more stable HDPE friction stir welding.
method: Simulate temperature, axial force, material flow and defects using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force histories.
Combine simulations and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free process windows.
evidence_signal: The CEL model agreed with experimental thermal, mechanical and void-formation observations, while ANN temperature and force predictions achieved R² values of 0.91–0.99.
watch_item: Predictive accuracy outside the tested process conditions remains unestablished; new operating ranges require experimental validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
